method: 100 questions (40 easy, 35 hard, 15 paraphrases, 10 cache traps) were each sent straight to the large model (openai/gpt-oss-120b) as the baseline, then through GreenPrompt with an empty cache, in file order. Local answers are measured as GPU power above idle; cloud answers use published per-prompt estimates. Where GreenPrompt did not use the large model, gemini-3.5-flash-lite compared its answer with the baseline answer, in random order, as better, same or worse, and said blind whether each answer was correct and adequate. Quality retained is the share of those judged answers rated same or better. Answers the large model gave itself were not judged.
limitations: Questions and labels were drafted with an LLM, then reviewed by hand (5 borderline training labels kept as they were).
Cloud energy and water are estimates (Google 2025 median prompt, range x0.5 to x2), not measurements; they are the same for every cloud answer, whatever its length.
Local energy counts the GPU only, not CPU, RAM or cooling.

An LLM judge can be wrong: in a hand check of 15 of its verdicts we agreed with 13. Where we disagreed, the judge had called a correct but shorter answer worse, so quality retained is, if anything, conservative.

Router tuning saw this set: training rows, the unsure band (0.10) and the meaning/length scaling were chosen while checking it, and a router trained on measured labels was rejected on it, so router accuracy here is not fully unseen. The router ignores trailing punctuation and case, so casually typed questions route the same as these.
The router is trained on 250 questions and its accuracy was still rising at that size, so some easy questions it is unsure about go to the large model (costs energy, not quality).
